subject: Re: MLFeatures pilot - capacity alignment and canary plan
messages:
From: Victor Gomez <victor@mlfeatures.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amy Lin <amy@mlfeatures.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MLFeatures pilot - token mix and pilot goals

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. Attached is a small token profile export we pulled from our staging instrumenter (mlfeatures_token_profile.csv) — it has a sample of 10k sessions and the prompt/response token distribution. A few quick notes:

- Expected steady-state QPS for the pilot: 8–12 RPS (user-facing inference requests), with a 2x burst allowance during promo windows.
- Prompt median ~ 220 tokens, prompt 95th ~ 800 tokens. Response median ~ 90 tokens, response 95th ~ 600 tokens.
- We expect ~45% of requests to be chat-style (multi-turn with KV cache) and ~55% single-shot generation.

Primary asks: can you provide a ballpark of dedicated GPU sizing for a 3-month pilot (non-production SLA, but <200ms p95 target)? Also interested in how Redwood would stage a canary/rollout — we'd like to limit blast radius while testing model variants.

We appreciate any breakout (GPUs, concurrency per GPU, suggested model family/quantization) and any caveats you see in the data.

Best,
Victor
Victor Gomez
Head of ML Engineering, MLFeatures
victor@mlfeatures.ai

Attachment: mlfeatures_token_profile.csv (csv, 82KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Victor Gomez <victor@mlfeatures.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: MLFeatures pilot - token mix and pilot goals

Victor — great profile, thanks for sending. Pasted a few quick observations and a high-level sizing hypothesis below.

On Mon, May 6, 2028 at 09:12, Victor Gomez <victor@mlfeatures.ai> wrote:
> Attached is a small token profile export ...
> Primary asks: can you provide a ballpark of dedicated GPU sizing for a 3-month pilot (non-production SLA, but <200ms p95 target)?

Summary observations:
- Prompt/response medians and 95th percentiles inline with conversational workloads we see in retail search assistants. 95th tail is non-trivial (up to ~1400 tokens total for roundtrips).
- 45% multi-turn means KV cache will be beneficial; we’ll size session pools differently than pure single-shot workloads.

Sizing hypothesis (ballpark):
- Suggested model family: rdx-7b-q4 (low-latency quantized variant) for the pilot; fallback to rdx-13b for high-quality user groups if we see quality regressions.
- Concurrency target: aim for 40–60 concurrent sessions per GPU for mixed prompt/response profile under q4 quant. This assumes smart batching and prefix cache.
- GPU mix: recommend starting with 2x A100s (or 3x A10s equivalent) for the pilot footprint to hit p95 <200ms with 8–12 RPS steady + 2x bursts.
- Cost/throughput caveat: if the 95th tail is very frequent, expect to need an extra GPU for headroom during promo bursts.

Canary/rollout suggestion (short):
1) Internal alpha: route 5% of traffic to pilot cluster running rdx-7b-q4 (monitor latency/cost/quality)
2) Quality probe: A/B 10% of alpha traffic to rdx-13b to validate quality delta on a representative prompt set (use Redwood Optimize eval set)
3) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 48–72 hours with automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency SLO misses.

Attachments / refs: I sketched a simple canary topology (pilot_canary_diagram.png) and added a HubSpot link for the deal.

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan: can you confirm whether MLFeatures prefers reserved capacity commit or a short-term Dedicated pilot (metered) so we can flesh pricing and SLA?
- Victor: any constraints on supported hardware/cloud region (we can map to A10/A100 availability)?

Thanks — happy to run a quick sizing workshop if you want to walk the numbers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan note: we should keep internal comms tight; Ben, can you prepare a short pricing sketch for a 3-month Dedicated pilot (2x A100 vs 3x A10 options) with a metered fall-back?

Victor — proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
- This week: Redwood provides a 1-page pilot sizing + cost sketch and a 3-step canary runbook (we'll include rollback thresholds). (Owner: Jordan / Ben)
- Next week: 60-minute workshop to validate assumptions against full token samples + traffic timeline (Owner: Marissa / Victor)
- Target start: 2028-06-01 (pilot live), 3-month duration, followed by capacity review.

Please confirm if the timeline works and if you can share preferred cloud regions (us-west1 / us-east1) — we'll map GPU availability and provide region-specific estimates. Also, if legal is ready for a short MOU, upload there; otherwise we'll circulate our standard pilot MOU for signatures (signed-mou.pdf).

If that all sounds good, I'll slot the workshop for next Thursday afternoon PT.
